source: Post-war Iowa records (1875 death / burial / census) — the survivor-who-died-young trail
rationale: Charles survived the war (mustered out Oct 1865) and moved with Alexander to Dover Township, Pocahontas County, Iowa by ~1870; he died there March 1875 of service-contracted disease. The defining post-war records are an 1870 census placing him in Iowa and an 1875 death record.

death_burial_1875.result: NOT FOUND in any open source — and the gap is STRUCTURAL, not exhaustion.
evidence: IAGenWeb Pocahontas County death indexes (http://iagenweb.org/pocahontas/deaths/deathindex.htm) begin Aug 26 1880 — 1875 PRE-DATES all extant county death-record coverage.
IAGenWeb / IowaGravestones Photo Project Pocahontas Co. Hubbell list: only 19th-c. Hubbell with a stone is brother Alexander F. (Cedar Twp, 1844-1894). NO Charles, no 1875 burial.
BillionGraves: 'No matches found' for Charles Hubbell d.1875.
Iowa WPA grave record (Pocahontas): a HUBBELL entry exists but the detail page is 403 -> handoff.
death_burial_1875.interpretation: Charles's 1875 grave is genuinely undocumented in free sources. He may lie in an unmarked or un-transcribed Dover-Twp/Pocahontas plot, OR the body/record returned to Clinton County NY. This is a real data gap, not a null that proves anything — flagged for handoff. (Contrast Henry, where a cemetery null was itself evidence.)

census_1870.collections: Ancestry '1870 United States Federal Census' (coll. 7163); FamilySearch 'United States Census, 1870' — target: Charles F. Hubbell, Dover Twp, Pocahontas Co., Iowa (likely with/near Alexander, mother Frances, sister Frances).
census_1870.value: Would place Charles in Iowa in 1870 (age ~30, born NY), corroborate the family migration, and — by his ABSENCE in 1880 — bound the 1875 death.

pension.collections: Ancestry coll. 4654 (General Index to Pension Files); Fold3; NARA T288.
pension.value: Charles likely filed his OWN invalid (soldier) pension for the service-contracted disease before his 1875 death; a mother's claim may follow. The invalid claim's medical affidavits could name the DISEASE — directly relevant to the cause-of-death question.

gar_suvcw.note: No GAR/SUVCW entry for Charles retrieved; brother Alexander carries a GAR star (separate).

notes: The single most valuable handoff for Charles is the PENSION file (names the disease) and the 1870 census (confirms the Iowa migration).
